newsitem.title: CAMBODIA: Cambodia royalists accuse partner of interference.
newsitem.headline: Cambodia royalists accuse partner of interference.

text.p: Cambodia's royalist FUNCINPEC party on Thursday accused its main coalition government partner of interfering in its internal affairs by supporting a dissident member of the party.

The accusation added to the political tension on the day exiled Prince Norodom Sirivudh left Hong Kong for Europe after an abortive attempt to fly home to contest charges that he plotted to kill Cambodian Co-Premier Hun Sen.

FUNCINPEC hit out against Minister of State Ung Phan for his statement on Tuesday blaming First Prime Minister Prince Norodom Ranariddh for deteriorating ties with its coalition partner, Hun Sen's Cambodian People's Party.
The two parties formed an uneasy coalition government after U.N.-run elections in 1993, which saw FUNCINPEC narrowly beat the incumbent CPP administration after years of war.

The CPP has backed criticisms made by Ung Phan, who said he and other unidentified FUNCINPEC officials no longer recognised the leadership of Ranariddh. The royalist party steering committee is expected to discuss Ung Phan's fate on Friday.
The five-page statement, which defended the prince against a host of charges of bad leadership, noted that CPP statements had specified Ung Phan's case was an internal matter for FUNCINPEC.

"However, the request made by CPP and its allied members (of smaller parties) to preserve the (government) position of Ung Phan, FUNCINPEC considers this as an interference in the internal affairs, which is unacceptable," it said.
The FUNCINPEC document noted that all the criticisms made by Ung Phan, a former senior CPP member who joined FUNCINPEC in 1992, had regularly been raised by Hun Sen.
It said Ung Phan's statement was "a result of an act well planned in advance by those pulling strings behind and simply executed by Ung Phan".
FUNCINPEC did not attach direct blame, but analysts believed the document was referring to Hun Sen, a former comrade-in-arms and close friend of Ung Phan.
Ranariddh called in the statement on all government offcials and military police to remain calm and neutral while continuing to serve the administration and protect the constitution.

The statement said FUNCINPEC had shown it was ready to share power in the interests of the nation, but warned its patience had limits in view of the "incessant provocations of some power-hungry individuals".

The Ung Phan case has created additional tension between FUNCINPEC and CPP, already high following a deadly March 30 grenade attack against a demonstration led by opposition leader and FUNCINPEC ally, Sam Rainsy.
Exile Prince Sirivudh meanwhile said Ranariddh and the FUNCINPEC supported his return to Cambodia.
A half-brother of King Sihanouk and a former foreign minister, Sirivudh went into exile in December 1995 after being held for a month on charges of involvement in an alleged plot to kill Hun Sen.
He said in Hong Kong he did not think he would be killed when he eventaully arrived in Cambodia.
"I believe in our institutions. We have a monarchy, we have a king, we have a national assembly, we have a royal government," he said.
